references.text: Abraham offers hospitality and sets food before his guests. Similarly, food is set before Abraham's servant, but the servant refuses to eat until he has delivered his message – a prioritization of duty over personal need.
David swears not to eat bread until the sun goes down, expressing a commitment that surpasses personal needs – a parallel to the servant's refusal to eat until he has spoken his errand.
Jesus says that his food is to do the will of him who sent him and to finish his work. This reflects the attitude of the servant in Genesis 24:33, where the mission takes priority over eating.
The proverb about the diligent one who shall stand before kings mirrors the servant's dedication to his mission – he does not let personal needs get in the way of his service.
